title: Standardize audit action ontology and field contract for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: produce a prescriptive audit event ontology and flat field contract for RBAC v2 changes and admin actions, plus a compact diff encoding that is storage-efficient and queryable. This ticket focuses on: 1) canonical action taxonomy (assign, revoke, role.create, role.update, policy.apply, permission.evaluate, escalation.detect, sso.link, sso.unlink, api-key.rotate, service-principal.create), 2) normalized actor/target fields (SSO identities, service principals, API tokens, system processes), 3) a compact, append-friendly diff format (opcode-style) for recording state changes to RBAC objects, and 4) redaction and retention rules for PII and secrets.

Acceptance criteria:
- A single-page contract (fields, types, cardinality, examples) agreed by security, infra, and PM.
- Action taxonomy with stable action identifiers and human-friendly labels.
- Actor and target canonicalization rules (how we map SAML/SCIM/SSO assertions to the actor.id and actor.subject fields).
- Diff encoding proposal showing typical operations (set, unset, add, remove, replace) and storage implications (size estimates for common ops).
- Backward compatibility plan with current audit consumers + migration notes.
- An initial implementation sketch and a draft schema document in Drive, with a linked PR stub for the runtime and the storage encoding layer.

Scope exclusions: not covering audit transport ingestion pipeline (separate infra ticket) and not implementing UI changes to Console (handled by console-2026.04).
event_examples: Example: role assignment change (flat JSON string): {"event_type":"rbac.role_assignment", "action":"role.assign", "timestamp":"2026-03-10T15:22:33Z", "actor_id":"urn:saml:userid:12345", "actor_type":"user", "target_type":"user", "target_id":"urn:saml:userid:67890", "role_id":"role:billing-admin", "outcome":"success", "client_ip":"52.47.23.10"}

Example: policy object update stored as compact opcode patch (string): [{"op":"replace", "path":"/policy/0/conditions/2/value", "value":"team:payments"}, {"op":"add", "path":"/policy/0/meta/tags", "value":"internal"}]

Example: service principal key rotation event: {"event_type":"service_key.rotation", "action":"api-key.rotate", "actor_id":"system:service-agent", "target_id":"sp:analytics-ingest", "rotation_method":"kms", "retention_tag":"sensitive", "outcome":"success"}
decision_log: 2026-03-11: Chose opcode-style patch (set/add/remove/replace) over full object snapshots to reduce storage and improve patch replayability. Tradeoff: slightly more complex consumer logic; mitigated by providing a small client library to materialize patches.

2026-03-12: Canonical actor identity will prefer SAML/SSO subject mapped to stable URN (urn:saml:<id>) with fallback to internal user id if mapping not present. Rationale: makes cross-system joins and user lookups deterministic for audits and investigations.

2026-03-12: Action taxonomy will use dotted identifiers (rbac.role.assign, rbac.role.revoke, rbac.policy.apply, auth.sso.link) with a human-facing label field for Console. This supports hierarchical queries and aggregation.

2026-03-12: Redaction rules: never store secrets (api keys, private keys); mask token fragments and store retention tags. PII fields (email) are allowed only when consented for audit and must be covered by retention policy. Implement sampling for high-volume system events (e.g., policy evaluation) with deterministic sampling key to ensure reproducible traces when needed.
open_questions: How do we version action taxonomy? Proposal: semantic-style integers (v1, v2) with name-to-id registry stored in config service.
Do we need a separate 'actor_context' field for SAML attributes (groups/roles) or should these be denormalized into metadata? Decision pending with PMs due to payload size concerns.
What query patterns will SRE use against audit storage? Need input to optimize indexing strategy for actor_id, target_id, action, and timestamp.
Should we include both pre- and post-state snippets for certain sensitive edits (e.g., policy changes)? This increases storage but eases forensic analysis.
